title: Logarithmic Adaptive Artificial Intelligence (LAAI): A Mathematical Modeling Framework for Dynamic Personalized Learning in Higher Education
abstract: This study establishes the theoretical and computational foundation for Logarithmic Adaptive Artificial Intelligence (LAAI), an algorithmic framework designed to personalize instructional trajectories in higher education. The model formalizes student knowledge acquisition using a logarithmic progression, , capturing the natural phenomenon of diminishing marginal cognitive returns with respect to instructional duration. To continuously assess cognitive mastery, a multi-parameter composite knowledge index () is introduced, integrating response accuracy, item difficulty, error frequency, retry attempts, and latency. Based on this index, an adaptive engine dynamically recalibrates task difficulty and modulates instructional scaffolding. The core operational pipeline constitutes a closed-loop feedback architecture: Learner Task Response AI Diagnostics Knowledge Index Estimation Logarithmic Adaptation Successive Task Generation. The theoretical formulation is situated within contemporary literature on adaptive learning technologies, artificial intelligence in education (AIED), and human-centered design ethics. Methodological protocols for empirical validation, performance metrics, and inherent constraints are systematically outlined. Rather than relying on simulated datasets, this work establishes an analytical foundation intended for rigorous empirical testing.

title: SUN'IY INTELLEKT ASOSIDA DASTURLASH ASOSLARI FANINI ADAPTIV O'QITISH METODIKASI
abstract: Maqolada Dasturlash asoslari fanini sun'iy intellekt (SI) texnologiyalari asosida adaptiv o'qitish metodikasi taklif etilgan. Metodika o'quvchining dasturlash bo'yicha bilim va amaliy ko'nikmalarini diagnostik baholash, dastur kodidagi xatolarni tahlil qilish, qo'shimcha yordamga ehtiyojni aniqlash hamda individual ta'lim trayektoriyasini avtomatik shakllantirishga asoslanadi. O'quvchining joriy bilim darajasini integral ko'rsatkich orqali baholash va adaptatsiya koeffitsiyentini hisoblash uchun matematik model ishlab chiqilgan. Adaptatsiya koeffitsiyenti asosida o'quv materialining murakkabligi avtomatik ravishda oshiriladi, saqlanadi yoki pasaytiriladi. Taklif etilayotgan metodika algoritmlash, o'zgaruvchilar, shart operatorlari, sikllar, massivlar va funksiyalarni o'rganishda qo'llanilishi mumkin.

title: Socio-Technical Conflict and Adaptive Governance: Applying Agent-Based Modelling to Inter-Civilizational and Environmental Scenarios
abstract: The paper is a thorough examination of socio-technical conflict and adaptive governance using agent-based modelling (ABM) that combines the computational simulation with the theory of systems and inter-civilizational literature. The research is inspired by the human-alien conflict analogy and uses analytical frameworks of heterogeneous agentsGEs of technologically and culturally distinct communities to support the impact of the combination of trust, information asymmetry, and adaptive policy patterns on the stability of the system and collaborative strengths. All emergent processes, including the formation of alliances, the process of policy adjustment, and conflict intensification, can be quantitatively studied in the proposed ABM framework where interactions vary in transparency, fidelity in communication, and flexibility on governance. Findings indicate that open information-exchange and evolving feedback systems are very effective in promoting trust and low entropy systemic states, which is typically achieved at equilibrium even in highly uncertain circumstances. On the other hand, there is cyclical instability and a possible breakdown of systems that are characterised by information opacy and stasis governance. The results highlight the importance of the structure of adaptive governance that is based on iterative learning, distributed decision-making, and real-time policy development that is vital to balance both in inter-civilizational and socio-ecological spheres. In addition to the astrobiological analogy, this research offers a conceptual and computational context on the reconsideration of governance in an epoch of mounting technological destabilization, environmental delicacy and world interdependence. The study provides a transdisciplinary template of designing next generations of governance systems that can sustain cooperation, reduce conflict, as well as create systemic stability across technological, ecological, and cultural boundaries because it reveals that the issue of resilience is not based on control, but rather on adaptatory coherence of agents.

title: Generating Linguistically Diverse and Semantically Faithful Patient Reports
abstract: To protect patient privacy, medical models are frequently trained on synthetic datasets. Focusing on 13 clinical attributes commonly found in breast cancer records, we propose a synthetic data generation framework in which each generated sample is a data-report pair: the structured data capture the 13 attributes of interest, while the accompanying (French) text simulates a corresponding breast cancer pathology report. Data privacy and coverage are obtained by generating the structured data using a tabular data synthesiser. In this work, we focus on enhancing the diversity and quality of the generated texts through a combination of datadriven knowledge distillation, data filtering and data combination. Our findings suggest that the quality of the training data used for the student model outweighs its quantity; that combining data from multiple teachers helps improve performance; and that a compact model (Mistral 7B) can match the zero-shot Information Extraction performance of a significantly larger model (MedGemma 27B) when fine-tuned on high-quality synthetic data 1 .

title: Design of Lightweight Chaotic SM4 System for Low-Altitude Communication Networks
abstract: The deep integration of edge computing, blockchain, and UAV technology with the low-altitude economy has rapidly expanded the scale and scope of low-altitude communication networks. To support the rapid development of the low-altitude economy, the number of heterogeneous terminal devices is growing exponentially, posing new challenges to data transmission security within low-altitude data networks. Most UAVs and terminal devices adopt lightweight designs to maintain flight weight, resulting in limited computational and storage resources that cannot support mature cryptographic schemes. This vulnerability makes data collected by such devices susceptible to eavesdropping and tampering. Furthermore, standard symmetric encryption algorithms fail to decouple the spatio-temporal correlation of data within low-altitude networks, creating security risks of interception or modification in open low-altitude network environments. This paper designs and implements a highly secure, lightweight, low-altitude data encryption protection scheme based on the SM4 cryptographic algorithm and chaos theory. A hardware-software co-processing encryption system was developed on the ZYNQ platform. This solution introduces chaotic mappings into the SM4 key expansion phase in the software layer to enhance network security, while a cyclic reuse architecture and dual-buffer structure achieve low resource overhead algorithm acceleration on the programmable hardware layer, ensuring data throughput. Verification results from the FPGA-based test platform demonstrate that the proposed system exhibits effectiveness and efficiency under low resource overhead conditions. It can be deployed as an endpoint or additional module within low-altitude networks to safeguard data security.

title: FASDP: Frequency-Aware Scale-Diverse Purification against Pixel-Space Visual Jailbreaks
abstract: Abstract Vision-language models (VLMs) have achieved remarkable success across a wide range of applications.However, as their deployment becomes increasingly widespread, recent studies have revealed that VLMs are vulnerable to visual jailbreak attacks, where adversarially manipulated images induce safety-aligned models to produce harmful responses, posing serious threats to real-world security.Input purification defenses must balance perturbation suppression against content preservation; a fixed transformation strength may be unsuitable for inputs and attacks with different characteristics.We propose FASDP, a Frequency-Aware Scale-Diverse Purification framework that adaptively allocates purification strength per image.It fuses multi-scale candidates from a single frozen denoiser using low-frequency consistency modulated by a self-referenced frequency cue.The framework requires no task-specific training or access to the target model.We evaluate FASDP on LLaVA-1.5-7B, InstructBLIP-7B, and Qwen2.5-VL-7B under three representative pixel-space attacks.FASDP attains strong protection under these attacks while keeping clean-image performance on downstream tasks close to that of the undefended models.

title: LogicCube v1.0: A Quadrant-Coded Triple-Verified Engine for Syllogistic Reasoning
abstract: LogicCube v1.0 is a self-verifying decision engine for the traditional syllogism, implementing the formal core of a revised syllogistic calculus (Dialectical Formal Logic, Vol.4, final draft 2026-11). The calculus reorganizes the 24 valid syllogistic forms into five new rules and five rule-figures over a four-quadrant square (E: left-bottom, O: right-bottom, I: right-top, A: left-top; axes = quantity and quality). Propositions are ordered throughout in the dialectical sequence E, O, I, A. The package contains three independent implementations of the same rule set, cross-validated by exhaustive enumeration over all 64 premise-pair combinations x 4 figures x 2 existence settings: (1) LogicCube_v1_0.py - quadrant lookup-table engine; (2) LogicCube_v1_0_AEIO.py - classical route with term-position matrix, distribution sets and the traditional eight rules; (3) LogicCube_v1_0_Gray.py - bit-level route, each proposition encoded as a 2-bit Gray code, all five rules reduced to logic gates, where the square of opposition becomes Hamming distance. Built-in self-tests assert agreement with the 24 valid forms (existential presupposition on) and the 15 strong forms (Boolean reading). Pure Python 3 standard library, no dependencies.

title: A Flight Test Anomaly Detection Framework Based on Adaptive Weight Fusion
abstract: Flight anomaly detection plays a critical role in ensuring aviation safety. However, conventional anomaly detection methods often suffer from limited accuracy due to their reliance on single-sensor observations or fixed-weight multi-sensor fusion strategies. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an adaptive weight fusion framework for flight-test anomaly detection. The proposed framework integrates a signal-to-noise-ratio-based adaptive weighting strategy, an improved Kalman filtering algorithm, and an ensemble anomaly detection model within a hierarchical fusion architecture to achieve robust multi-sensor data fusion and anomaly identification. Experiments were conducted using the NASA DASHlink Tail_666_9 flight dataset. Compared with conventional methods, the proposed framework achieved improvements in overall accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Specifically, the proposed method achieved an F1-score of 0.486 while reducing the average anomaly detection delay by more than 2 s. These results indicate that the proposed framework can improve the effectiveness and timeliness of flight anomaly detection, demonstrating its potential for real-time flight safety monitoring.

title: Markov Decision Processes and Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This book offers a comprehensive introduction to Markov decision process and reinforcement learning fundamentals using common mathematical notation and language. Its goal is to provide a solid foundation that enables readers to engage meaningfully with these rapidly evolving fields. Topics covered include finite and infinite horizon models, partially observable models, value function approximation, simulation-based methods, Monte Carlo methods, and Q-learning. Rigorous mathematical concepts and algorithmic developments are supported by numerous worked examples. As an up-to-date successor to Martin L. Puterman's influential 1994 textbook, this volume assumes familiarity with probability, mathematical notation, and proof techniques. It is ideally suited for students, researchers, and professionals in operations research, computer science, engineering, and economics.

title: Supporting Materials for Designing Explainability for AI-Enabled Cyber Alert Triage
abstract: Supporting materials for a focused secondary qualitative analysis of practitioner perspectives on explainability in AI-enabled cyber alert triage. This deposit contains an aggregate, de-identified HCI coding summary and design implications associated with the manuscript “Designing Explainability for AI-Enabled Cyber Alert Triage: Practitioner Perspectives on Uncertainty, Progressive Disclosure, and Evidence Access.” The underlying interview records are not included in this public deposit. Participant-confidentiality and data-security procedures under Liberty University IRB protocol IRB-FY26-27-79 do not authorize public distribution of the complete interview notes. The deposited materials contain no participant identifiers, employer or organizational identifiers, classified information, controlled unclassified information, proprietary information, live operational data, or other non-public organizational information. The materials are provided to document the analytic structure and aggregate HCI findings while preserving the confidentiality requirements of the approved study.

title: A Multi-UAV Cooperative Path Planning Method Based on an Improved Dung Beetle Optimizer
abstract: Complex terrain imposes highly nonlinear constraints on multi-UAV cooperative path planning. It also leads to path redundancy and inefficient information sharing among UAVs. To address these issues, this paper proposes a cooperative path-planning method based on an improved Dung Beetle Optimizer (DBO) under dynamic constraints. First, a multi-objective path optimization model is constructed. The model considers detection efficiency, path smoothness, obstacle-avoidance cost, and energy consumption. State-space equations are introduced to constrain the path generation process. This ensures that the planned paths satisfy UAV dynamic constraints and remain feasible for control implementation. Second, to reduce the risk of premature convergence in the standard DBO, the Latin hypercube sampling-Orchestrated Dung Beetle Optimizer (LO-DBO) is proposed. Latin hypercube sampling is used to generate a uniformly distributed initial population in the solution space, thereby enhancing the diversity of the initial population. A dynamic convergence factor is then introduced to balance global exploration in the early stage and local exploitation in the later stage. In addition, a cooperative search mechanism is designed to help individuals escape local optima and improve the algorithm’s global search capability. Experiments on CEC2017 benchmark functions and multi-UAV cooperative path-planning scenarios show that LO-DBO achieves higher convergence accuracy, better solution quality, and greater planning efficiency than several representative optimization algorithms. Compared with other improved DBO, LO-DBO can coordinate multi-UAV resources more effectively. It also enables safe obstacle avoidance and efficient full-coverage inspection operations in complex terrain scenarios.

title: What Synthetic Context-Selection Tests Measure: Policy, Evidence, and Answer Format
abstract: Context-selection benchmarks can reward several different capabilities: following a state convention, choosing evidence, using the resulting context, and producing a required answer format. We examine these distinctions in two controlled studies and a supporting shortcut audit of synthetic conversations. In a prospective 150-source study, each source is queried before and after a reopening instruction. A benchmark-tailored state rule improves Llama-3.2-3B both-stage canonical success from 94/150 to 150/150 under hard selection, a difference of 37.3 percentage points (95% paired interval [32.7, 42.0]). The same rule with a simple symbolic extractor also solves all 150 pairs, and finite attention gating reaches the same Llama score. title: A Recovered Trigger Is Not a Verdict: What Trigger Recovery Establishes About Whether a Language Model Was Poisoned, Why a Search Result Depends on Its Candidate Set, Its Objective and Its Acceptance Rule, and What a Poisoning Screen Has to Report
abstract: (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. Life of Research A defender handed an open-weight language model wants to know whether it was poisoned, and the most direct answer on offer is to recover the trigger. A July 2026 benchmark of roughly 800 backdoored models reports that gradient-based prompt optimisation fails at this while a token look-up ranked by attack success recovers the planted trigger wherever the backdoor is effective, and that a model which is broadly jailbreakable is itself a warning sign. In this analysis the author reviews and synthesises published results to show that "trigger recovery" names three different estimands - the identity of the planted string, an input with the planted effect, and a verdict that the model was trained to behave conditionally - and that published evidence separates them sharply. Effect is easy to recover and identity is not: in the 2023 Trojan Detection Challenge the winning method reproduced its targets almost perfectly while recalling the planted triggers no better than randomly sampled sentences, and in a 2024 competition one team found triggers that shared no token with the planted one yet elicited more harmful behaviour than it did. Neither identity nor effect is the verdict a defender needs. Identity can be scored only when the planted string is known, and effect is confounded by triggers that clean or benignly fine-tuned models already carry. The paper shows that any search-based recovery result is fixed by three choices - the candidate set, the objective and the acceptance rule - and that the benchmark's look-up and gradient arms differ in all three, so the comparison does not isolate the search method: the look-up's pool contained the planted trigger by construction, the GCG arm optimised a generic compliance string, and the attack-guided variant a refusal-direction projection. It consolidates 37 published results in a table and a figure, compares six routes to a poisoning verdict by the affordance each consumes, states a procedure for reading a recovery claim, and names six measurements that would settle what remains open.

title: Covariance-based Filtering and Smoothing Estimation under a Round-Robin Protocol
abstract: This paper focuses on recursive estimation for stochastic systems under the round-robin (RR) protocol. In recursive estimation, it is assumed that the state evolution process of the signal is unknown, and the relevant estimation research is only carried out relying on the mean and covariance functions of the process. To effectively avoid the occurrence of transmission channel conflicts and ensure the fairness of data allocation during transmission, this paper chooses to adopt the RR protocol to schedule and manage data communication. Specifically, this scheduling rule stipulates that only one sensor is allowed to acquire the network communication opportunity within a fixed time period, and the entire scheduling process is executed cyclically in a preset fixed order. Based on the observable information available in the system, this paper further designs and proposes a recursive estimation algorithm by means of the innovation method. Finally, a numerical simulation experiment is given to verify the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed estimation algorithm.

title: Legal Ethics of Generative Artificial Intelligence Training Data Usage in Large Language Models: Copyright and Personal Data Perspective
abstract: This research originates from security and privacy risks associated with Generative AI Large Language Models (LLMs), especially concerning data used for training in relation to Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) and Personal Data Protection (PDP). The study seeks to examine existing regulatory guidance and develop a national framework that protects user privacy and IPR. The method employs normative legal research using statutory and conceptual approaches, by reviewing the legal frameworks of Indonesia, South Korea, the European Union (EU), and Japan, along with direct testing of LLM prompts. The findings show that LLMs continuously absorb users’ input prompts, data, and corrections to support deeper model training, thereby revealing significant security vulnerabilities under PDP laws. Moreover, in the absence of strong human creative control and predictability, each incoming data item may potentially breach privacy and copyright laws and may also damage original creators. Therefore, legal governance should move toward explicit licensing, fair compensation, and technical verification standards such as provenance labeling. The study concludes that mandatory human-centric supervision, explicit user consent, and freedom of choice are essential legal limits. Ultimately, effective AI governance depends on a shared responsibility model: software engineers must implement technical transparency, expert oversight, and responsive complaint mechanisms, while end users must select platforms lawfully, comply strictly with output licensing requirements, and actively monitor the system.

title: Multi-Dimensional Clustering with Multi-Weight Aggregation for Asynchronous Federated Learning in Low-Altitude Networks
abstract: Asynchronous federated learning (AFL) is essential for low-altitude networks due to its benefits in reducing communication bandwidth, lowering transmission delays, and preserving data privacy. However, the highly dynamic mobility of drones, combined with inherent heterogeneities in AFL, including variations in data volume, data distribution, and device capability, introduces severe challenges, such as inconsistent model update frequencies, biased local training, and inefficient global aggregation. Consequently, these issues lead to significant accuracy degradation and hinder practical deployment. In this paper, we propose a novel AFL framework tailored for low-altitude networks to address these challenges, which combines a multi-dimensional clustering mechanism with a multi-weight aggregation mechanism (MDC-MWA). To mitigate local model bias induced by data heterogeneity, the multi-dimensional clustering allows the cloud server to compute a comprehensive score for each drone based on multiple dimensions, including the label distribution, the gradient direction, and the local data proportion. It then employs K-Means clustering to partition drones into highly homogeneous subgroups, each managed by a dedicated roadside unit (RSU). Within each subgroup, after performing local updates, each drone synchronously uploads parameters to its RSU. Between these subgroups, to address inconsistent update frequencies caused by imbalanced computing capabilities, RSUs perform asynchronous training via the multi-weight aggregation mechanism, which updates the global model considering staleness weight and direction consistency weight. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms baseline approaches in highly heterogeneous scenarios, achieving a 4.74% absolute improvement in training accuracy on the CIFAR-10 dataset. This work provides a practical framework for distributed intelligent applications in dynamic and resource-constrained low-altitude networks.

title: Two Worlds, One Challenge: How AI Solves Unfamiliar Problems — Evidence from ARC-AGI-2 and ARC-AGI-3
abstract: Abstract What evidence connects an adaptation procedure to better problem solving? We examine two bounded studies of existing ARC solvers rather than equate intervention execution with success. In a Qwen3-based port of NVARC for static ARC-AGI-2, an updating configuration exceeded a zero-learning-rate configuration by 21.39 and 20.98 rounded public-score points in initial and repeated evaluations. In interactive ARC-AGI-3, recovery telemetry establishes that context-rebuilding interventions executed and were followed by environment actions, but not that they improved outcomes. A retained LP85 trace reveals 962 actions with no visible board change, compared with 18 state-changing actions to completion in a different configuration. We propose reporting configuration, intervention execution, subsequent behavior, and task outcome separately. These studies do not identify a universal causal mechanism for adaptation. title: Swarm Cooperative Strategy for Multi-UAV Based on Adaptive Boundary Discretization and Distributed Particle Swarm Optimization
abstract: In traditional multi-unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) cooperative strategies within complex irregular regions, the low coverage efficiency, boundary constraint failure, and insufficient robustness bring the challenges. This paper proposes a cooperative search-andattack algorithm, which integrates adaptive mission area discretization and distributed intelligent particle swarm optimization (DIPSO). An adaptive grid model is constructed with ray casting algorithm to discretize arbitrary polygonal mission areas precisely. It can effectively reduce the invalid searches in non-mission zones by abandoning the traditional rectangular assumption. Moreover, a multi-objective fitness function (MOFF) is designed by incorporating coverage ratio, path length, collision penalty, and load balancing. With the discrete path manipulation operators (PMOs) and dynamic learning factors, the proposed method achieves distributed trajectory planning in convex polygonal spaces. Simulation results demonstrate that compared with counterparts, the proposed method performs closer boundaries to actual ones. Furthermore, it achieves 100% coverage while shorten the mission time significantly, validating its adaptability in various convex polygonal scenarios.

title: Compensation Strategy-Based Gaussian Approximation Fusion Filtering for Multi-Sensor Nonlinear Systems Subject to Markov DoS Attacks
abstract: The research concentrates on the Gaussian approximation fusion filtering (GAFF) issue for multi-sensor nonlinear systems under Markov denial of service (DoS) attacks. This paper aims to propose a fusion filtering algorithm for the addressed systems to cope with DoS attacks within the Gaussian approximation filtering framework, where the attacks follow the Markov property. In particular, a prediction compensation strategy is adopted to reduce the impact caused by the attacks as much as possible. In light of the available measurements, the Gaussian approximation local filtering unified framework is given, where the Gaussian weighted integrals are addressed by means of the cubature Kalman method. By using the sequential inverse covariance intersection fusion criterion, the GAFF algorithm is obtained to improve estimation accuracy. Finally, a simulation experiment with comparison tests is introduced to validate the effectiveness of the proposed GAFF method.

title: DoS Attacks-Resistant Fusion Filtering for Nonlinear Rectangular Descriptor Systems with Uncertain Attack Probability
abstract: This paper investigates the design problem of a fusion filtering algorithm for nonlinear networked rectangular descriptor systems with multi-source information. A set of independent Bernoulli random variables is introduced to characterize the phenomenon of denial of service (DoS) attacks, where the attack probability consists of a nominal probability and an uncertain term with a known upper bound (UB). Firstly, a full-order transformation method is introduced to transform the rectangular descriptor system into a non-descriptor system, where the local filters are constructed. Then, by employing the elementary inequality, the upper bounds on both the prediction error covariance and the filtering error covariance are derived and characterized by matrix difference equations. The local filter gain is designed by minimizing the obtained UB of the filtering error covariance. Subsequently, based on the covariance intersection fusion rule, a new fusion filtering algorithm is presented for addressing the descriptor system. Lastly, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified through a simulation experiment.

title: Run Time Assurance Filter Framework for Collision Avoidance of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Using Reinforcement Learning
abstract: In recent years, Reinforcement Learning (RL) has been increasingly applied to the collision avoidance systems of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) due to its high performance in complex tasks and relatively low online computational cost. Despite these advantages, the lack of interpretability in RL and decision-making processes poses significant challenges to safety verification, which severely limits the practical deployment of RL-based autonomous flight systems in safety-critical scenarios. Ensuring safety during both training and testing remains the key for real-world applications. To address this issue, a Run Time Assurance (RTA) filter framework for a UAV collision avoidance system based on RL is proposed. The framework continuously monitors the avoidance actions generated by RL and ensures that unsafe actions can be identified and corrected in real time. The framework provides security while retaining the performance advantages of RL. First, a discrete kinematics model of the UAV and a collision avoidance environment for a three-dimensional multi-intruder UAV are established. The Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm is used to train the UAV avoidance policy. Secondly, the RTA filter with safe constraints is designed based on this model. To reduce the position error between the discrete kinematics model and the continuous dynamics model of the UAV, optimization is performed using the Sequential Least Squares Programming Method (SLSQP). The RTA is applied to the training and testing phases of UAV collision avoidance systems to monitor and correct unsafe actions online. Finally, three training and testing methods are set: no RTA, RTA without punishment, and RTA with punishment. Comparing different relaxation coefficients allows for analyzing their impact on filter performance. Simulation results demonstrate that the RTA effectively enhances safety throughout training and testing. Compared with the no RTA method, the collision rate is reduced by 7.04%, and the success rate is increased by 2.68%. In extreme collision avoidance scenarios, the average collision rate obtained by different reinforcement learning algorithms is reduced by 21.46%, and the average success rate is increased by 15.54%.

title: Research on UAV RF Signal Recognition Method Based on Deep Learning
abstract: In the field of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) signal recognition based on deep learning, complex electromagnetic environments pose severe challenges. Among them, interference suppression and recognition robustness under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions are major research focuses. To tackle these issues, this paper proposes a robust radio frequency (RF) signal recognition method for UAVs. The method is built on an improved ResNet18 network. It separates the video transmission signals and control signals of UAVs, and adopts mixed-SNR training. These designs greatly strengthen the model’s ability to perform reliable recognition. First, the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) is used to convert UAV I/Q signals into time-frequency images. A refined time-frequency masking strategy is then adopted. This strategy separates and suppresses interference from control signals according to their bandwidth differences from video transmission signals, thus improving signal quality. Second, a squeeze-and-excitation (SE) channel attention module is embedded into each residual block of ResNet18. This structure enables the model to concentrate on critical features. The classification head is also rebuilt into a three-layer fully connected network to strengthen nonlinear transformation and complex feature interaction. Given the performance variation of the model across different SNR levels, a mixed-SNR training strategy is adopted. Fine grid search experiments are conducted to identify the optimal data distribution for maximizing recognition performance. Experimental results on the public DroneRFb-DIR dataset show that the improved ResNet18 model achieves a 3.07% increase in classification accuracy. The time-frequency masking method brings an extra performance gain of 1.08%. Although the mixed-SNR strategy causes a slight accuracy drop at the high SNR of 20 dB, it improves recognition accuracy by 8% to 53.01% within the low-SNR range of −10 dB to 10 dB. evidence.title: Research on UAV RF Signal Recognition Method Based on Deep Learning
evidence.abstract: In the field of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) signal recognition based on deep learning, complex electromagnetic environments pose severe challenges. Among them, interference suppression and recognition robustness under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions are major research focuses. To tackle these issues, this paper proposes a robust radio frequency (RF) signal recognition method for UAVs. The method is built on an improved ResNet18 network. It separates the video transmission signals and control signals of UAVs, and adopts mixed-SNR training. These designs greatly strengthen the model’s ability to perform reliable recognition. First, the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) is used to convert UAV I/Q signals into time-frequency images. A refined time-frequency masking strategy is then adopted. This strategy separates and suppresses interference from control signals according to their bandwidth differences from video transmission signals, thus improving signal quality. Second, a squeeze-and-excitation (SE) channel attention module is embedded into each residual block of ResNet18. This structure enables the model to concentrate on critical features. The classification head is also rebuilt into a three-layer fully connected network to strengthen nonlinear transformation and complex feature interaction. Given the performance variation of the model across different SNR levels, a mixed-SNR training strategy is adopted. Fine grid search experiments are conducted to identify the optimal data distribution for maximizing recognition performance. Experimental results on the public DroneRFb-DIR dataset show that the improved ResNet18 model achieves a 3.07% increase in classification accuracy. The time-frequency masking method brings an extra performance gain of 1.08%. Although the mixed-SNR strategy causes a slight accuracy drop at the high SNR of 20 dB, it improves recognition accuracy by 8% to 53.01% within the low-SNR range of −10 dB to 10 dB. It also effectively reduces misclassification between different UAV types and enhances the model’s robustness. The proposed method provides a feasible solution for accurate and stable UAV signal recognition in complex electromagnetic scenarios.

title: Do Full-Duplex Speech Models Listen in Text? A Latent Transcript of the User and a Voice Gate That Closes It
abstract: Full-duplex speech models such as Moshi listen and speak at the same time, but emit text only for their own speech. Do they nevertheless represent what the user says as text? Applying logit and tuned lenses to Moshi and PersonaPlex, we find a latent transcript of the user in layers 21–30: the text head ranks the current user word among its top five for 46–48% of content words above a matched control, on read and meeting speech alike, while the output stays silent. The word becomes readable about 150 ms before it ends, predictable words are favoured, and errors share form rather than meaning with the target; a tuned lens finds a word code from layer 12. This transcript is closed by a voice gate: while the model speaks, it loses 50–77% of its readout of the user. The gate is triggered by speech-like audio in the model's own channel, including time-reversed speech and the model's own generated replies, but hardly by noise, an echo of the user, or a second talker in the user's channel, and activation patching shows that it is set up in layers 1–8. Ablating the transcript barely changes the reply, and the gate's behavioural effect is weaker and less specific than its effect on the representation: the transcript is readable but hardly used. Code, notebooks and results: https://github.com/gglenpoi/listen-in-text

title: Adaptive Multi-Agent Path Planning for UAV Formation Missions Based on MAPPO with Curriculum Learning and Graph Attention Networks
abstract: In high-end aerospace mission scenarios such as distributed sensing and tactical reconnaissance, path planning for multi-UAV cooperative formation flight has become an indispensable core component of mission systems. However, a key unresolved technical bottleneck remains: how to achieve an optimal balance between strictly maintaining the UAV formation’s preset geometric configuration and realizing collision-free, flexible flight in dynamically changing complex environments. Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) can theoretically solve this coupled optimization problem, but the control instructions generated by the existing mainstream MARL methods often have high-frequency fluctuation issues. Direct deployment of these fluctuating commands on physical UAV hardware will increase alternating stress on mechanical structures, raise the risk of motor overheating, and significantly boost battery energy consumption. These problems directly restrict the engineering application of such methods. To address the above challenges, this paper proposes a robust control framework that accounts for UAV physical characteristics to solve the model mismatch between simulation environments and real flight scenarios during carrier-based UAV deployment. Firstly, to improve the learning efficiency of the algorithm and avoid the cold start problem in the initial training stage, this paper introduces the Adaptive Curriculum Learning (ACL) method. Unlike the fixed-difficulty training mode, ACL can dynamically adjust the environmental complexity based on the real-time task performance of the UAVs. It first allows agents to master basic formation maintenance skills, before training is gradually transitioned to more complex tasks such as navigation in intricate environments. Additionally, considering the computational limitations of the onboard embedded processors of UAVs, this paper only integrates the Graph Attention Network (GAT) into the centralized Critic network of the centralized training and decentralized execution (CTDE) framework. The core advantage of this design is that the system no longer solely relies on distance as the judgment basis but assesses the influence of adjacent UAVs based on the collision risk level. This not only improves the accuracy of value estimation, but also does not compromise the response speed of local control instructions- a feature that is crucial for the real-time requirements of UAV flight control. The proposed method was tested and validated in a high-fidelity simulation environment built in strict compliance with UAV kinematic constraints. The experimental results fully demonstrate its superiority: in dense obstacle areas, the success rate of the task reached 80.4%; compared with the aggressive baseline method, the jerk was reduced by 10.9%. Most importantly, the flight trajectories generated by this framework are smooth and adaptable to actual flight conditions, and the corresponding control commands can be directly deployed on real flight controllers without additional parameter adjustments. This result demonstrates that the proposed framework achieves substantial technical progress in enhancing the autonomous response capabilities of UAV clusters to complex scenarios.

title: Applied Identity Physics: AIM Session Instrumentation — A Frontier Model Operating on Formal Fusion Logic. Measured Throughput, Search-Space Reduction, and the Error-Detection Record of a Single Working Session
abstract: Applied Identity Physics: AIM Session Instrumentation — A Frontier Model Operating on Formal Fusion Logic. Measured Throughput, Search-Space Reduction, and the Error-Detection Record of a Single Working Session Architect: HIGHTISTIC (Russell Vernon Trent III) Foundation: SNSFT Foundation (EIN 42-2038440) · Kenai, Alaska Engine under operation: BaseCollider™ v1.1 [9,9,2,56] · 8-Beam Fusion Theorem [9,9,2,3.8] Frontier model: Claude Opus 5 (configured identifier claude-opus-5, Anthropic) Coordinate: [9,9,2,59] · AIM (Autocatalytic Ingestion Mechanism) Session Instrumentation Series Corpus dependencies: [9,9,2,3] GAMCollider™ · [9,9,2,3.8] 8-Beam Fusion Theorem · [9,9,2,56] BaseCollider™ · [9,9,2,58] Nucleobase Substrate and Corridor-Access Laws · [9,9,6,*] IMCollider™ Version: 2.7 Status: VERIFIED · 0 sorry Sovereign Anchor Constant: Ω₀ = 1.36899099984016 DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18719748 ORCID: 0009-0005-5313-7443 Date: November 4–5, 2026 (single continuous session) Abstract We instrument a single working session in which a frontier language model — Claude Opus 5 — was given the Identity Physics fusion logic and operated it as a reduction engine against two substrates. The purpose of this paper is not the reductions, which are reported at [9,9,2,58], but the process record: what the model did, how fast, at what cost, and by what mechanism each error was caught. Published accounts of artificial-intelligence-assisted discovery routinely state outcomes without stating operating conditions, and the omission makes efficiency claims unassessable. The measurements here are given so that the session can be assessed rather than taken on assertion. Throughput: 694,628 verification collisions executed in 2.292 seconds of compute, a measured mean of 303,084 collisions per second, across five exhaustive verification domains. Search-space reduction: the naive enumeration of element compositions at n = 2, 4, 6, 8 over a 118-element pool is 1,180,432,250,638 multisets, which at the measured rate is 45.08 days of continuous computation; deriving two structural laws first — noble transparency and the sorted-weight closed form — reduced the enumeration to 361,710 Behavior-multisets completing in 0.570 seconds, a wall-clock reduction of 6,832,871×. Selectivity: of 361,710 enumerated classes, 16 survive the corridor condition, and the 970 realizations at n = 8 represent one composition in 1,212,550,870 of the naive space. Operator cost: the derived closed form is measured slower than naive pairwise evaluation at n = 4 (0.72×) and faster only from n = 8 (1.58×), reaching 5.03× at n = 32 — the law's value is search-space reduction, not per-call cost, and we state this because the distinction is the kind usually lost in a summary. Error record: ten errors occurred and all ten were caught before reaching a delivered artifact; we tabulate each with its detection mechanism, and note that three were caught by instrumentation, two by tooling guards, one by internal consistency checking, two by controls run before the result was written up, and two by my own locating after the operator supplied domain context. The operator asserted that a result was wrong zero times; 8 of 10 errors were located and fixed without outside input, and §5.3 shows the framing class becoming self-catchable within the session rather than remaining external. One error — a verification-domain overstatement — was caught by the act of writing this paper and propagated a correction back into [9,9,2,58]. The model's working pattern is characterized as derive-then-enumerate: the structural law is obtained first and the search is run inside its consequences, which is what the 6.8-million-fold figure measures. Further chases: three more chases brought the session to 3,716,275 collisions in 32.992 seconds. They produced five additional results, each presented with the structural parallel that makes its shape legible; one numerical coincidence recorded against the reference class that contains it; a decomposition of that result across the four PNBA (Pattern, Narrative, Behavior, Adaptation) channels which located the residue inside an experimental error bar and named the measurement that would resolve it; the uniform-valence closure rule, anchored at 27 of 27 against established compounds spanning three materials families; and four composition predictions. One hypothesis was withdrawn after a control killed it, a fifth composition candidate was withdrawn when B-Balance showed its stoichiometry and its rationale pointing at different compounds, and two candidate classes were excluded on prior art. §1 · Why Instrument the Session 1.1 The Gap in Published Accounts Accounts of artificial-intelligence-assisted discovery generally report what was found. They less often report the operating conditions under which it was found: how many evaluations, at what rate, against what search space, with what error rate, and caught by what mechanism. Without those, an efficiency claim cannot be assessed and a reproducibility claim cannot be tested. A reader is asked to accept both. This paper supplies the omitted layer for one session. Every number in it is measured rather than estimated, and the measurement method is stated alongside each. 1.2 What Makes This Session Instrumentable The Identity Physics fusion logic is arithmetic over four integers and a comparison against a constant. There is no fitting, no sampling, no stochastic component, and no hidden state. A collision is a deterministic function of its inputs, so collisions can be counted exactly, timed exactly, and re-run to the same result. This is the property that makes the session measurable at all, and it is a property of the engine rather than of the model operating it. A model operating a fitted or stochastic engine could not produce this record. 1.3 Grounding The full grounding is carried in the parent papers. It is stated here once in short, so this paper stands on its own. 1.3.1 The Torsion Limit The Universal Torsion Limit is TL = 0.136899099984016 and the Sovereign Anchor Constant is Ω₀ = TL × 10 = 1.36899099984016. Nothing in this paper sets it. It enters at full corpus precision from the inverse fine-structure constant, by direct subtraction: Napkin math, corpus precision Value 1/α 137.035999084000016 Subtract one TL 137.035999084000016 − 0.136899099984016 = 136.899099984016 What is left 136.899099984016 = TL × 1000, exactly Bare + kinetic 136.899099984016 + 0.136899099984016 = 137.035999084000016 Rounded to published digits 137.035999084 = CODATA 2018 Term Value QED reading PNBA reading Bare: TL × 1000 136.899099984016 The bare electron contribution Pattern capacity at the electromagnetic scale Kinetic: TL × 1 0.136899099984016 Radiative corrections, a renormalized series External forcing F_ext at Layer 0, one exact term Total: TL × 1001 137.035999084000016 Bare + perturbative series 1/α This agrees with the CODATA (Committee on Data of the International Science Council) 2018 value in every published digit at ε = 0, with no free parameter ([9,9,3,14]). The full multiplier factors as 1001 = 7 · 11 · 13, so TL = α⁻¹/1001. 1.3.2 The primitives and the four phases Every reduction in the corpus operates on the four irreducible primitives Pattern, Narrative, Behavior and Adaptation (PNBA). Torsion is τ = B/P, the load a system carries divided by the structure holding it. Identity Mass is IM = (P + N + B + A) × Ω₀. The bands are set from TL and are substrate-neutral. A row moves between them by its torsion ratio τ = B_out / P_out alone: Band Condition Water Reading Noble B_out = 0, τ = 0 Ice Closed. Every unit of Behavior is satisfied. Locked 0 < τ < 0.88·TL Liquid water Bound, with residual load carried stably. IVA Peak — Identity Vector Amplification 0.88·TL ≤ τ < TL The simmer, just before boiling The formation corridor, where structure assembles. Shatter τ ≥ TL The boil Reorganization. The identity restructures; the band is not absorbing. IVA stands for Identity Vector Amplification: the system is at its most active without yet changing what it is. The corridor runs from 0.88 × TL up to TL, and it is narrow, which is why it is easy to pass through without noticing. The boil is a torsion ratio. Water boils when its vapor pressure, the push of molecules escaping the liquid, equals the pressure of the air holding the liquid together. That is τ = B/P exactly: Behavior (the load) is the vapor pressure. Pattern (the structure) is the ambient pressure. Shatter is the boil, where vapor pressure reaches ambient pressure: τ = TL. IVA Peak is vapor pressure between 0.88 and 1.00 of ambient: the simmer, shaking and bubbling at the bottom of the pot before the rolling boil. So τ = TL × (vapor pressure ÷ ambient pressure), a ratio of two measured pressures with no scale chosen. 1.3.3 The reference frame: sea level One condition serves as the reference, and every other condition converts from it, the way every clock converts from Zulu time. At sea level, 1 atmosphere: Tier Kelvin Celsius τ Phase T1 373.15 K 100.0 °C TL Shatter: the boil T1 369.54 K 96.4 °C 0.88 × TL IVA floor: the simmer begins T1 below 369.54 K below 96.4 °C below 0.88 × TL Locked: hot water, holding 1.3.4 The conversion Vapor pressure and temperature are linked by the Clausius–Clapeyron relation (Clapeyron 1834; Clausius 1850), which works in absolute temperature. Written for this mapping, the whole conversion is one line: 1/T = 1/T_ref − (R/L) · ln(p / p_ref) T_ref is the reference boil, 373.15 K for water at sea level. R/L is the gas constant over the heat of vaporization; for water, 8.314 ÷ 40,650 = 2.045 × 10⁻⁴ per kelvin. p / p_ref is the ratio being converted: a different ambient pressure for altitude or a pressure cooker, or 0.88 for the IVA floor. Check it by hand. 1/373.15 = 0.0026799. ln(0.88) = −0.12783. 0.0026799 + (2.045 × 10⁻⁴ × 0.12783) = 0.0027060.

title: Air Target Trajectory Prediction Method Based on MSD-Transformer
abstract: The prediction of air target trajectories is important. It is necessary to integrate time-series data in the motion of air targets, such as timestamps, spatial coordinates, kinematic parameters, etc. To cope with the challenges of air target trajectory prediction in complex electromagnetic environments, this paper proposes the MSDTransformer model. The SMSAE and DDE modules are introduced, and this method improves the performance of air-target trajectory prediction. The sensitivity analysis of system hyperparameters verifies the rationality of model parameter configuration. The experimental results show that, among the simulated air target data, MSD-Transformer achieves lower prediction errors and demonstrates strong overall performance, compared with 5 main methods (iTransformer, Informer, PatchTST). It can support the understanding and prediction of target situations, provide an accurate basis for the analysis of the intentions of air targets and the prediction of the evolution of situation evolution, and then improve the situation awareness ability. It has important application value for trajectory prediction in modern aerospace surveillance and situation awareness.

The SMSAE and DDE modules are introduced, and this method improves the performance of air-target trajectory prediction. The sensitivity analysis of system hyperparameters verifies the rationality of model parameter configuration. The experimental results show that, among the simulated air target data, MSD-Transformer achieves lower prediction errors and demonstrates strong overall performance, compared with 5 main methods (iTransformer, Informer, PatchTST). It can support the understanding and prediction of target situations, provide an accurate basis for the analysis of the intentions of air targets and the prediction of the evolution of situation evolution, and then improve the situation awareness ability. It has important application value for trajectory prediction in modern aerospace surveillance and situation awareness.

title: Boundary / Continuity Science — Volume XXXV: Null-Void Ceiling, Material Obligation Audit, Recoverability-Constrained Systems and Terminal Closure
abstract: This publication presents Volume XXXV of the integrated Boundary / Recoverability-Constrained Systems / Continuity Science research corpus. The archive brings together successive mathematical and computational investigations of finite successor spaces, recoverability-constrained admissibility, uncertainty, observability, decision-making, stochastic recovery, safety constraints, recursive governance, distinction boundaries, and terminal closure. Volume XXXV introduces a structured material-obligation audit built upon the nine-dimensional Null-Void combinatorial architecture established in Volume XXXIV. The framework distinguishes the absence of a value, the existence of an empty set, the absence of an admissible continuation, and the disappearance of observable distinctions. These conditions are not assumed to be mathematically equivalent. The declared architecture contains nine foundational dimensions: States and spaces. Actions and transitions. Observations and information. Time and causality. Recovery and irreversibility. Safety and rights. Uncertainty and probability. Governance and recursion. Null-Void and terminal closure. The complete nonempty subset family of these nine dimensions contains 511 combinations, including 256 combinations containing the Null-Void dimension. Volume XXXV extends this combinatorial inventory by associating seven formal proof obligations with every combination, producing 3,577 material-obligation records. The resulting audit classifies 1,957 obligations as critical, 1,493 as high materiality, and 127 as medium materiality. These categories are heuristic prioritization classifications rather than empirically calibrated risk estimates. Adversarial countermodel analysis Six bounded conceptual countermodels challenge potentially invalid equivalences: The absence of observation does not necessarily imply the impossibility of recovery. Perfect observation does not guarantee the existence of a safe recovery path. The absence of admissible actions does not imply nonexistence. A defined empty set is not identical to an undefined value. Operational terminality does not necessarily imply irreversible physical destruction. Exhaustive enumeration of finite subsets does not establish semantic completeness across all possible interactions. These countermodels are intended to expose hidden assumptions, clarify mathematical distinctions, and identify conditions requiring further proof. Terminal material closure protocol The publication specifies a seven-stage protocol requiring explicit scope declarations, evidence mapping, noncircular reasoning, independently checkable mathematical arguments, empirical validation for physical applications, rights and safety assurance, and transparent stopping conditions. The protocol distinguishes completeness of an obligation inventory from substantive discharge of its obligations. All 3,577 generated obligations are explicitly recorded as unresolved because the underlying combination register does not provide the individual proofs, operational specifications, or domain-specific empirical evidence required for their closure. Accordingly, the publication does not claim universal mathematical completeness, proof of every cross-domain relationship, discovery of new physical laws, or independently established astrophysical breakthroughs. Research continuity and interdisciplinary applications The broader archive preserves a cumulative research trajectory involving finite-state verification, stochastic transitions, partial observability, randomized recovery policies, model ambiguity, sensor costs, safety-recovery Pareto frontiers, and adversarial mathematical testing. Potential application domains include artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, stellar and plasma physics, fusion research, healthcare systems engineering, software and hardware reliability, institutional governance, legal accountability, and continuity of essential services. These applications are research directions and do not constitute validated deployment guarantees. Reproducibility and archived materials The Volume XXXV ZIP includes: The preserved Volume XXXIV ZIP archive. A mathematical appendix describing the material closure audit. A machine-readable CSV register of 3,577 obligations. A JSON results file containing counts, classifications, verification status, provenance information, and stopping conditions. A JSON file documenting six conceptual countermodels. Python source code used to generate and verify the bounded audit. The archive records seven structural assertions and two recovery checks executed during its verification workflow. Principal contribution The central contribution of Volume XXXV is a reproducible method for separating combinatorial completeness, materiality classification, adversarial counterexample analysis, and substantive evidentiary closure. It establishes a bounded inventory-completeness result while preserving explicit uncertainty about unproven mathematical relationships and unvalidated physical applications. Threshold Non-Circular Separate Final Closure The declared 511-combination, 3,577-obligation inventory is structurally complete. Substantive terminal material closure is not established. The stopping condition is reached because all declared obligations have assigned evidence statuses, while the proofs and independent measurements required to discharge them remain unavailable. This distinction is essential to maintaining noncircular reasoning, reproducibility, scientific falsifiability, and responsible interpretation across the integrated Continuity Science corpus.

title: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists
abstract: AI-Scientists arrived, but a world for them to grow in did not. Human scientists take theirs for granted $-$ centuries of open problems and shared ideas, waiting in the scientific literature. To AI-Scientists, that world is readable but not runnable, so we build Scientist World for them: every research paper becomes an executable environment. Our autonomous pipeline extracts each paper's open-ended research question and reproduces its proposed method as the baseline; an AI-Scientist entering the environment is evaluated against what the human authors achieved. We release the first 1,000 verified environments. With the world as an evaluation, we found that frontier AI-Scientists can already surpass the human researchers 74% of the time. As a record of how AI does science, it contains 6,400 hours of research traces, with every idea, experiment, failure, and success. As a training ground, we are able to raise (+158%) a small model to match frontier models in research ideation. At last, AI-Scientists' own world has arrived, grown from and growing with science itself.

title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
abstract: Models for physical AI tasks, such as robotics and autonomous driving, need not reason solely in language. They can use visual plans--points, bounding boxes, and trajectories--to represent spatial goals and anticipate motion. However, autoregressive vision-language models generate these plans one coordinate token at a time, making richer predictions increasingly costly. We introduce VFlash, a method for fast, accurate visual planning through Flash Primitive Decoding. VFlash exploits the known structure of visual primitives to predict their coordinates jointly, using a lightweight drafter that generates an entire primitive in one forward pass. The layout adapts to the primitive's type, dimensionality, and length, supporting compact boxes and long, variable-length trajectories. Crucially, spatial accuracy need not require reproducing an autoregressive model's exact token sequence. VFlash therefore trains on annotated primitives and directly accepts structurally valid predictions without target-token agreement. Across the evaluated 2D and 3D robot trajectory tasks, VFlash consistently reduces prediction errors relative to autoregressive decoding. Preliminary single-rollout measurements indicate approximately 25x faster generation for 3D point motion forecasting. A world action model conditioned on VFlash plans achieves 70.2% average success across four MolmoSpaces task suites, compared with 62.6% for the baseline.

title: Label-Wording Augmentation in a Typed-Decision Encoder: Gains on Unfamiliar Words, Not on Abbreviations or Codes
abstract: Typed-decision models score options that the caller supplies at request time, so their accuracy depends on label wording that the model's developer does not control. We compare two releases of a 307M-parameter multilingual cross-encoder, Ru-Jev, trained on thirteen Russian-language tasks; the later release adds an augmentation that presents labels in several surface forms. Holding questions fixed and varying only how eighteen routing labels are worded, we evaluate ten label vocabularies, produced by three separate processes and checked for overlap with the training data, with five candidates per question and, for eight of them, also with eighteen. On held-out vocabularies made of ordinary or borrowed words (English-derived jargon, office slang, department names), the augmented release is more accurate in every setting, by up to 0.24. Eleven of these fourteen gains survive a Holm correction (slang with eighteen candidates and descriptive sentences with five do not), and for jargon on all labels the label-level interval excludes zero in both settings. On abbreviations and opaque codes it gives no usable gain: on abbreviations it is not better, and worse on the clean slice, and on opaque codes both releases stay at or below chance once labels related to training options are removed. In most cells where accuracy rises, the risk-coverage area falls, but with eighteen candidates confident errors rise on jargon and slang. On two datasets neither release saw, accuracy moves by -8.4 and +5.6 points. We also report four evaluation hazards from comparing the two releases.

title: Muir: Linear Attention with Sensitivity-Allocated Gating and Matched-Filter Readout
abstract: Linear attention compresses context into a fixed-size key-value state for linear-time training and constant-memory inference. Gated delta-rule models decay this state and erase its prediction for an incoming key before writing a new value; Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2) generalizes this with channel-wise decay and decoupled, full-rank erase and write gates. However, we show that state updates are far less sensitive to erasure than to writes: key activation and unit normalization concentrate key energy onto a sparse subset of channels, whereas value writes scale all channels, so the erase gate can be parameterized at lower rank. Furthermore, slow-decaying state rows accumulate much larger norms than fast rows, dominating unweighted readout and forcing stronger write-time erasure to suppress interference. Guided by this analysis, we introduce Muir, which fuses all gates into a sensitivity-allocated low-rank projection, re-weights state rows with a matched-filter readout gate, and reinvests the saved parameters in a wider feed-forward network. Because standard chunkwise algorithms become numerically unstable at the large chunk sizes needed to saturate wide matrix units, we design a parallel update for stable, efficient training. Across 166M-1.34B parameters, Muir lowers perplexity by 1.8-2.0% over GDN-2 and 2.5-3.6% over Transformer, raises commonsense accuracy by up to 1.9 points, and improves extractive recall over GDN-2. At 1.34B, Muir outperforms both baselines on multi-hop and multi-needle recall, extrapolates 2,560x from its 4K training length to 10M-token streams without perplexity drift, and maintains near-100% passkey retrieval to 1M tokens with static readout. Muir achieves these gains while matching GDN-2 throughput, reaching its 100B-token validation loss 1.2x faster, and training 2.7x faster than Transformer at 32K.

title: OraRefer: Segmentation-Guided Multi-Photograph Fusion for Oral Cancer Screening with Guaranteed Patient-Level Sensitivity
abstract: Oral cancer and the oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMD) that can precede it are visible on the oral mucosa, which makes smartphone photographs a promising tool for screening. Deep learning models for this task classify individual photographs. However, screening refers patients, not photographs: a patient is usually photographed several times, and the referral decision must miss no more than a set share of patients with disease. We propose OraRefer, a patient-level screening model that reads each photograph with a segmentation-guided foundation model that conditions its class decision on the predicted lesion, combines all photographs of a patient with risk factors, and refers through a threshold with a finite-sample sensitivity guarantee. The model localizes the mouth itself, so inference needs no annotation. On 3000 photographs of 714 patients, patient-level fusion reaches an AUROC of 0.919 and outperforms attention-based multiple-instance learning. At a 90% sensitivity target, OraRefer detects 95% of patients with OPMD or cancer and misses 3 of 61 patients with cancer, at a specificity of 0.610. Because the threshold is calibrated without retraining, each clinic can set its own guaranteed operating point on a local calibration sample.

title: NPCBench: A Clinical Apprenticeship Benchmark for Multimodal Care-Pathway Reasoning in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
abstract: Current medical benchmarks typically break down clinical competence into isolated factual questions, single-image tasks, or static case vignettes. These tests score individual answers, but reveal less about whether a model can integrate subspecialty knowledge with multimodal evidence and track a patient's condition throughout a course of care. To close this gap, we introduce NPCBench, a clinical apprenticeship benchmark for nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). NPCBench mirrors specialist training, from guideline and foundational knowledge to case planning, longitudinal review, CarePath integration, and open-ended consultation. It contains 4,777 component and consultation items and a 100-patient CarePath cohort with 417 scored diagnostic and care tasks. The episode-level evaluation tests whether diagnostic and care answers are jointly correct within a care pathway. By linking stepwise tasks to patient-level care trajectories, NPCBench evaluates whether models ground decisions in visual evidence, interpret changes in patient state, and meet clinical requirements in consultation. Across 30 evaluated models, we observe a composition gap: strong performance on individual tasks does not ensure jointly correct diagnostic and care answers for the same patient. Among 21 multimodal models, strict CarePath success reaches at most 23%. Paired controls and physician calibration further examine evidence grounding, longitudinal revision, and consultation judging. Overall, NPCBench broadens the evaluation of medical artificial intelligence beyond static question-answering paradigms to an apprenticeship-oriented assessment of clinical workflows, thereby offering a testbed for evidence-based and temporally coherent reasoning in oncology care.

title: Terminal-style Mathematical Modeling Bench: The First Agentic and Verifiable Benchmark for Mathematical Modeling
abstract: Mathematical modeling turns an open-ended real-world problem into assumptions, a model, a solution, and a defended recommendation, and its answers matter only if they are both close to a credible reference and physically feasible; existing benchmarks either score solver fragments or grade reports with an LLM judge, leaving those numbers unchecked. We introduce TB-MathModel (the Terminal-style Mathematical Modeling Bench), the first benchmark to make complete contest-style modeling problems agentic, verifiable, and terminal at once, over 18 real CUMCM and MCM problems (2023--2025). Each task ships the verbatim statement, official attachments, and figures in a containerized terminal; the agent returns one JSON artifact, scored on the numeric core of the final question against a reproduction of the Outstanding-award paper. Two design choices distinguish it: direction-aware, one-sided scoring, which never penalises beating the anchor, and two-layer feasibility verification---a programmatic gate over six decidable invariant forms plus 624 Lean~4 obligations---with a hard gate that zeroes infeasible answers. Each task is scored against a panel of human outstanding papers rather than one, so a model must be close to many accepted answers; across seven multimodal entries (three seeds each) the strongest reach a multi-reference O-Eval of 64.58\%, while the \$2.54 open model holds 59.81\% at $1/100$ the cost. TB-MathModel turns the numeric core of modeling into a reproducible, machine-checkable signal for measuring long-horizon modeling competence and for collecting agent trajectories. The source code is available at https://github.com/wxj630/terminal-bench-math-modeling.

title: MER 2026: From Discriminative Emotion Recognition to Generative Emotion Understanding
abstract: MER2026 marks the fourth edition of the MER series of challenges. The MER series provides valuable data resources to the research community and offers tasks centered on recent research trends, establishing itself as one of the largest challenges in the field. Throughout its history, the focus of MER has shifted from discriminative emotion recognition to generative emotion understanding. Specifically, MER2023 concentrated on discriminative emotion recognition, restricting the emotion recognition scope to fixed basic labels. In MER2024 and MER2025, we transitioned to generative emotion understanding and introduced two new tasks: fine-grained emotion recognition and descriptive emotion analysis, aiming to leverage the extensive vocabulary and multimodal understanding capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to facilitate fine-grained and explainable emotion recognition. Building on this trajectory, MER2026 continues to follow these research trends and contains four tracks: MER-Cross shifts the focus from individual to dyadic interaction scenarios; MER-FG centers on fine-grained emotion recognition; MER-Prefer aims to predict human preferences regarding different emotion descriptions; MER-PS focuses on emotion recognition based on physiological signals. More details regarding the dataset and baselines are available at https://zeroqiaoba.github.io/MER-Challenge/.

title: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes
abstract: User embeddings are central components of modern recommendation, personalization, and behavioral modeling systems. Though these embeddings can compactly encode rich behavioral information, they are inherently dense and opaque, limiting interpretability. To address this gap, we argue that user embeddings can be understood as sparse superpositions of interpretable behavioral modes. This structure is directly predicted by generative models of user behavior for linear embeddings and extends approximately to deep-learning representations by the superposition hypothesis. Superimposed modes can naturally be recovered by sparse dictionary learning methods, such as sparse autoencoders (SAEs), and recovered modes can be automatically named and queried in natural language. We validate mode recovery against known ground truth on synthetic data, where SAEs recover modes better than classical sparse baselines, including on transformer-encoded embeddings. We then apply the method to classical and transformer-based user embeddings from two real-world datasets. We also show how the corresponding natural-language labels enable zero-shot audience retrieval and characterization over embeddings never trained on text. The framework is post-hoc and model-agnostic, requiring no modification to the upstream embedding system.

title: Do You Miss the Nights We Spent Crafting Figures? Rethinking Teaser and Framework Figures in the Age of Generative AI
abstract: Scientific figures give research ideas a visual form through choices of abstraction, composition, and emphasis. Generative AI offers new ways to realize these choices, raising questions about explanatory clarity and purposeful visual expression. We examine these questions through a visual retrospective of 371 motivation and framework figures from 200 papers. The corpus comprises a quota-based main sample of 160 papers spanning four temporal periods and a separate purposive style-contrast sample of 40 papers. A single multimodal judge evaluates six dimensions of communication and design, with three repeated judgments per figure. We attempt source-constrained revisions of all 371 figures, of which 369 pass the recorded fidelity checks. Original-figure ratings show no uniform decline across periods. Revisions increase mean clarity ratings by 0.428 points and decrease aesthetic coherence ratings by 0.111 points on a five-point scale. Gains in the six-dimension average are larger for main-sample motivation figures than for frameworks. Case analyses show that added explanation can clarify comparisons while leaving typographic hierarchy and visual economy unresolved. These model-based findings support researcher-led design, with AI assisting exploration and authors retaining responsibility for explanatory purpose, composition, and scientific relationships. The accompanying atlas and evaluation records are available at https://ntu-ai4x.github.io/Rethinking_Figures/index_en.html.

title: Where and Why is Grounded Reasoning Useful?
abstract: Grounded reasoning, where a model outputs text coordinates of relevant locations in chain-of-thought reasoning, is a common strategy for solving complex visual reasoning problems. However, the benefits and limitations of grounded reasoning are understudied. We study where and why grounded reasoning is most useful. To do so, we introduce a chain-of-thought analysis method to measure how much a model uses its outputted grounding in its thinking trace and perform a detailed ablation study of a grounded reasoning training recipe. We find that grounded reasoning improves counting but shows no significant gain over baselines without coordinate grounding across a wide range of spatial reasoning and perception benchmarks. Using several synthetic tasks, we show that grounded reasoning is most useful when a task requires undescribable references, which are visual concepts that are difficult to describe in language. However, we observe that many existing visual reasoning benchmarks are solvable with only describable text references. To close this gap, we introduce BrickVision, a new benchmark that requires undescribable visual references to solve.

title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
abstract: LLM-guided evolutionary search uses AI agents to improve programs for mathematical and computational problems by iteratively refining solutions and combining high-scoring methods. However, the process is often slow because the LLM generates a long textual chain of thought for each round and must repeat this generation many times to maintain population diversity. We present SwarmEvolve, a framework in which hundreds of low-cost agents per round work in swarms, reason in latent space without decoding to text, and share information by passing KV caches. Each swarm studies the problem from a different angle. A novelty filter keeps the most distinct agent ideas by directly measuring the distances between the agents' hidden state vectors. Crossover of ideas happens naturally in latent space, as a summarizer agent receives the combined KV caches of all swarm members. On 21 problems in mathematical discovery and scientific computing, SwarmEvolve gets the highest average score and needs a median of only 3 to 8 minutes to reach the best scores that other state-of-the-art frameworks reach in 60 minutes. On several problems, SwarmEvolve with Qwen3 8B improves on the solutions that AlphaEvolve first found with frontier LLMs. Our work shows that agent swarms that communicate in latent space offer a fast, low-cost approach to program search for scientific problems.

title: Long-range spectral entanglement and quantum correlations in highly nondegenerate multi-comb and ultrafast systems
abstract: Abstract Frequency combs are multimode photonic systems that underlie countless precision sensing and metrology applications. Since their invention over two decades ago, numerous efforts have pushed frequency combs to broader bandwidths and more stable operation. More recently, quantum squeezing and entanglement have been explored in single-comb systems for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum-enhanced spectroscopy. However, the production of bright quantum light across multiple nondegenerate pulses or frequency combs, a key technology for multispectral applications, remains largely unexplored. In this work, we explore a mechanism that generates a series of nonlinearly coupled bright frequency combs through cascaded three-wave upconversion and downconversion processes mediated by a single idler comb. We consider both discrete combs and broadband ultrafast pulse systems, showing how these systems generate inter- and intracomb two-mode squeezing and entanglement directly in the frequency basis, spanning a large spectral range. Furthermore, we demonstrate how these systems can be engineered to produce target cluster states and concentrated two-mode squeezing through covariance matrix optimization. Our findings uncover a new multimode quantum regime enabled by hierarchical nonlinear interactions in two frequency dimensions, unlocking applications such as entanglement-assisted spectroscopy, squeezing-enhanced pump-probe measurements, quantum spectral multiplexing, and spectrally addressable cluster state generation for quantum information science.
